summary: Wanganui Airport serves the city of Whanganui on the southwest coast of New Zealand's North Island, near the mouth of the historic Whanganui River. It functions primarily as a regional general aviation facility, supporting flight training, private operations, and occasional scheduled services to Auckland. The airport sits on the coastal plain with easy access to the surrounding farmland and river valley.
faqs:
Q: What airlines operate scheduled flights from Wanganui Airport?
A: Scheduled passenger services to Auckland have historically been operated by Air New Zealand under the Link brand, though service availability should be checked directly with the airline as regional routes can change.

Q: How far is the airport from Whanganui city centre?
A: The airport is located approximately 5 km southeast of the city centre, typically a 10-minute drive.

Q: Does the airport have car rental facilities?
A: Car rental services are generally available in Whanganui city rather than directly on-site, so arranging pickup in advance is recommended.

Q: Are there customs and immigration facilities for international flights?
A: No, Wanganui Airport does not have international customs facilities and operates solely as a domestic airport.
transport_tips: Taxis and rideshare services provide the most convenient access to and from the airport, with the short drive into town costing only a few minutes. Visitors arriving without pre-arranged transport can phone a local taxi company upon landing. Having a rental car collected from town offers flexibility for exploring the wider Whanganui region and river road.
local_tip: If you're a flying enthusiast, time your visit to coincide with one of the local aero club fly-in events — the airport has an active GA community and the surrounding flat coastal terrain makes for excellent cross-country flying conditions.
